analysis:
Documentation-only changes in docs/provider/cli-reference.md for darkbloom sandbox setup. The setup command gains a repeatable --disk <volume> work-disk option (head lines 1256 and 1270). Disk checks are documented at lines 1286-1301: statfs on the path or its nearest parent, the /Volumes/<name> mount match, and APFS with ownership on. An optional ownership fix runs `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` in the terminal's foreground process group, so sudo reads the password and the CLI never does. Setup never formats a drive. Other changes cover the drive-choice prompt (1312-1324), passing --disk to the installer (1379), rerun behavior (1405), plan disks parsing and failure handling (1441-1450) and the status disks member (1527).

Relevant threat IDs are TB-013, A-019 and T-061, because the installer and add-on run as the Mac's owner. The documentation still says the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS (line 1307-1308); that is pre-existing and already covered by T-061. Setup refuses running under sudo (line 1280). The new sudo step only runs a fixed diskutil command against a path the operator chose, after an explicit prompt whose default is no. These edits documented no new privileged path that takes adversarial input.

The add-on's work-disk data lives outside the provider's attested boundary and is separate from the T-041 prefix-cache storage; no provider cache semantics change. Workflow changes in sandbox-disk.

Open questions for integration: verify that the SandboxWorkDisk.swift implementation builds the diskutil argument from the validated volume path as an argv element, not through shell interpolation. Also confirm that installer argument passing for --disk uses argv, not a shell string. Neither implementation file was supplied in this batch, so these points are unverified, not findings. The threat model's TB-013 could note the new sudo diskutil step.
